mint.description: The mint analysed, or empty string when AMBIGUOUS/INSUFFICIENT_DATA before resolution

bias.description: The directional trading view; give one unless AMBIGUOUS/INSUFFICIENT_DATA

setup_quality.description: How clean the setup is given liquidity, holders, tape and structure

key_levels.description: Concrete levels from the candles and liquidity (support, resistance, VWAP, range high/low, invalidation level)

size_hint.description: Size framed as a fraction of risk capital with the stop (e.g. '0.5-1% risk, stop below the range low'); never a dollar amount or a token count

missing_data.description: Sections or fields that were unavailable/null (copied from the dossier `availability.missing` and `knownUnavailable`). Empty array when everything was present. A non-empty list lowers confidence but — as long as price or liquidity exists — never forces INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

rug_probability.description: rug-check only: model's probability that this token rugs within 72 h

summary.description: Two to four short lines for a 40-column panel: the call in plain words and the deciding facts. Never repeats bias/levels/invalidation/size (rendered from their own fields), never a disclaimer line

candidates.description: AMBIGUOUS only: the mints the symbol could mean

results.description: When the answer is a LIST of coins (e.g. after a filter, or 'best setups right now'), put one entry per coin here by mint. The app renders a live table from these mints (prices/liq/vol come from its data layer, never your text); only mints already on screen or fetched via tools are shown. Give a one-line reason per row.

mint.description: base58 mint of a coin that is on screen or that a tool returned

reason.description: one short line on why this coin is in the list

filter_applied.description: When you called show_in_screener for a plain-language request, echo the structured filter you applied here so the user sees (and can correct) the numbers you chose.

query.description: the exact filter string you passed to show_in_screener, in dexterm grammar (e.g. 'mcap < 5M liq > 50K h24 > 0 flag:clean')

notes.description: the numbers you chose for vague words, in words (e.g. 'low cap = mcap < 5M; liquid = liq > 50K; up on the day = h24 > 0; not a rug = flag:clean')
